candidate_interface_supplied_by_coordina.systems: Finite-dimensional B and arbitrary reference R
candidate_interface_supplied_by_coordina.channel: CPTP Phi on B with faithful fixed state sigma, Phi(sigma)=sigma
candidate_interface_supplied_by_coordina.state_constraints: rho_B=sigma and D(rho_RB || rho_R tensor sigma)=I(R:B)_rho<=C
candidate_interface_supplied_by_coordina.target: Dimension-free control tending to zero with b of (1/2)||rho-(id_R tensor Phi^sharp Phi)(rho)||_1, using the same unrotated Phi^sharp for all eligible rho and R

strongest_imported_result.source: Junge, Renner, Sutter, Wilde, Winter, arXiv:1509.07127v3, Theorem 2.1 and Remark 2.2, Eqs. (17)-(21)
strongest_imported_result.exact_interface: D(rho||omega)-D(Nrho||Nomega) bounds the fidelity error of a single beta_0-averaged rotated-Petz recovery map depending on (omega,N), not rho.
strongest_imported_result.specialization: For omega=rho_R tensor sigma and N=id_R tensor Phi, stationarity makes the entropy loss equal to I(R:B)_rho-I(R:B)_(id tensor Phi)(rho). Product locality makes the averaged recovery factor as id_R tensor a fixed B map depending on (Phi,sigma), independent of rho_R.
strongest_imported_result.does_not_close: The premise is small entropy loss, not small trace residual b with merely bounded total I. The recovery map is a rotated-Petz average, not the unrotated Phi^sharp in the target.

decisive_missing_lemma: For every fixed C, prove a dimension-free g(C,b)->0 such that (1/2)||rho-(id_R tensor Phi^sharp)(rho)||_1<=g(C,b) under the candidate assumptions. Contractivity then yields target <= b+g(C,b).

negative_diagnostic_scope.claim: Bounded I(R:B) and b->0 do not force the relative-entropy loss I(R:B)_rho-I(R:B)_(id tensor Phi)(rho) to vanish dimension-freely.
negative_diagnostic_scope.construction: Classical rare-sector example in REPORT.txt with sigma(0)=1-p, sigma(i)=p/N, rho diagonal perfectly correlated, and Phi replacing each rare label by uniform rare output.
negative_diagnostic_scope.asymptotics: p log N->c>0 gives D->c, b=p(1-1/N)->0, and entropy loss p log N->c.
negative_diagnostic_scope.scope_limit: This example has Phi^sharp Phi=Phi, so target error equals b; it is not a counterexample to the candidate theorem.

other_sources.source: Sutter, Fawzi, Renner, arXiv:1504.07251v3, Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.4, Appendix F
other_sources.limit: CMI-controlled universal rotated/swiveled recovery from a marginal; no stationary-channel trace-residual interface. Appendix F does not refute the main Petz fidelity inequality.

other_sources.source: Brandao, Harrow, Oppenheim, Strelchuk, arXiv:1411.4921v4, Theorem 1 and discussion of Eq. (9)
other_sources.limit: CMI lower bounds optimized measured-relative-entropy reconstruction; the transpose-map numerics concern strictness/equality, not the candidate trace-norm implication.

other_sources.source: Salzmann, Bergh, Datta, arXiv:2405.01532v1, Theorem 5.1, Proposition 4.2, Theorem 7.2
other_sources.limit: Approximate fixed-point repair perturbs both state and channel; QMC proximity is dimension-dependent; local multi-state fixing obstructions have different quantifiers. Candidate already assumes exact stationarity.

novelty_statement: No exact imported theorem or counterexample to this supplied interface was identified in this bounded source pass. This is not evidence of priority or novelty.
early_falsification_test: Search or construct a finite-dimensional family with faithful exact stationary sigma, bounded I(R:B), b->0, and a nonvanishing unrotated backward residual (1/2)||rho-(id tensor Phi^sharp)(rho)||_1. A family of that form refutes the candidate; the classical information-tail family only refutes the entropy-loss shortcut.
